chapter: Sharkey, Chicago and the hot men
title: Emmett Hardy's style and Bix imitators
summary: Discussion of Emmett Hardy's playing, his copying of Bix Beiderbecke, and Red Nichols as a Bix imitator.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Emmett Hardy? Yeah, Emmett Hardy. What style did he play?

What style did he play? Emett Hardy. Yeah, Emmett Hardy. What style did he play? Emett Hardy. Yeah, Emmett Hardy. Just like for anybody else. Did he play like a... Just like for anybody else. A Joloba style? No, just anybody.
Poor Emmett didn't last for one. He wasn't going. Like Charlie? Same way, he just had good rhythm. Sorta like that. He had a Grodin style though, wasn't it? That's all. That's all.
It wasn't a Big Spiderback style, was it? No, Big Spiderback, no.
None of that was... He tried to copy off Big Spiderback, you know what I mean? That's what you tried to do. You never used to like that, remember you? Still do. Used to like that.

Still do. Greatest trumpet player that ever lived. I see him. Don't tell me this sometime, eh? No, he does. He died when he was 29, 1929. That's Red Nichols. Red Nichols, yeah. Another one they tried to copy. Yeah. But Red, I think he's the worst copier of all. Who? Here Red Nichols is the worst copier of Bix. Bix has got some imitators that are terrific.
